exercises.title: DNSSEC 1 — Read the real chain of trust
exercises.problemHtml:
labflow.test's chain, read from the bottom up (lab/out/c35-chuoi; long signatures cut):

$ dig +dnssec +noall +answer labflow.test A
labflow.test.		300	IN	A	203.0.113.10
labflow.test.		300	IN	RRSIG	A 13 2 300 20261201102442 20261101092442 62671 labflow.test. tHgSYhKgL+Va+d31K7R/x1uYqtxMlg+HMxogV0sVgsGPq67oXpbYhlkk o…
$ dig +noall +answer labflow.test DNSKEY @203.0.113.53 | awk '{ print $1, $4, $5, $6, $7, substr($8, 1, 16) "…" }'
labflow.test. DNSKEY 257 3 13 Q8ELEP109JcZSFib…
labflow.test. DNSKEY 256 3 13 xzRWnqoxiH8ysNNF…
$ dig +noall +answer labflow.test DS @192.0.2.20
labflow.test.		3600	IN	DS	30957 13 2 0FA2C679E930C7E36936706B14EAA9991CE9A57532C3620D014E2ABA F1499185
$ dig +noall +answer labflow.test DNSKEY @203.0.113.53 | dnssec-dsfromkey -a SHA-256 -f - labflow.test
labflow.test. IN DS 30957 13 2 0FA2C679E930C7E36936706B14EAA9991CE9A57532C3620D014E2ABAF1499185
$ dig +noall +answer test DS @192.0.2.10
test.			86400	IN	DS	39072 13 2 CCEC87AE6F412C58CF2EBA7C3DACC5B8CF14016F1AD8077617142FB5 01826AF1
$ cat /dnsz/anchor.conf
trust-anchors { . static-ds 57466 13 2 "53274C60181AAFF3C55E9752CA22148C8E40E807A4D2DB4602C10AA45C5E364B"; };
$ dig labflow.test | grep -E '^;; flags'
;; flags: qr rd ra ad; QUERY: 1, ANSWER: 1, AUTHORITY: 0, ADDITIONAL: 1
$ delv -a /dnsz/anchor.conf labflow.test A 2>&1 | head -2
; fully validated
labflow.test.		300	IN	A	203.0.113.10
$ delv -a /dnsz/anchor.conf static.labflow.test A 2>&1
; fully validated
static.labflow.test.	300	IN	CNAME	labflow.cdn.test.
static.labflow.test.	300	IN	RRSIG	CNAME 13 3 300 20261201102442 20261101092442 62671 labflow.test. vGKkGtZCt3kGalcf1Rto34AVEbuGFrAvZUfMHBPkiyku4DHl…
; unsigned answer
labflow.cdn.test.	60	IN	A	203.0.113.10

This set has 5 questions. There is nothing to run: answer in the panel on the right and press Submit. Work each one out yourself first (on paper or in the lab), then check — every explanation after Submit says why the tempting wrong answer is wrong.

Requirements

  • Answer every question in the answer panel, then press Submit.
  • All answers must be correct to get Accepted; the explanation of every question appears after you submit.

# DNSSEC 1 — Read the real chain of trust — answer key

1. In the RRSIG line "A 13 2 300 20261201102442 20261101092442 62671 labflow.test. …", what are the two long numbers?Trong dòng RRSIG "A 13 2 300 20261201102442 20261101092442 62671 labflow.test. …", hai con số dài là gì?
   Answer: c) Expiration then inception of the signature, in UTC
   Order: covered type, algorithm (13 = ECDSA P-256), labels, original TTL, EXPIRATION, INCEPTION, key tag, signer, signature. Here valid for 30 days; someone (or a job) must re-sign before the end.VI: Thứ tự: loại được ký, thuật toán (13 = ECDSA P-256), số nhãn, TTL gốc, HẾT HẠN, BẮT ĐẦU, key tag, người ký, chữ ký. Ở đây hiệu lực 30 ngày; ai đó (hoặc một tác vụ) phải ký lại trước khi hết.

2. DNSKEY 256 and DNSKEY 257: what is the difference?DNSKEY 256 và DNSKEY 257: khác nhau gì?
   Answer: a) 256 signs the records (ZSK); 257 signs the keys (KSK)
   The flags field: 257 has the SEP bit. Splitting the roles lets you change the ZSK often without touching the parent.VI: Trường flags: 257 có bit SEP. Tách vai trò giúp đổi ZSK thường xuyên mà không đụng tới vùng cha.

3. The DS at the TLD and the output of dnssec-dsfromkey are equal. What does that prove?DS ở TLD và output của dnssec-dsfromkey bằng nhau. Điều đó chứng minh gì?
   Answer: d) The parent vouches for exactly the key that labflow.test publishes
   DS = hash of the child's KSK, published and signed by the parent. Same key tag 30957, same digest — only the space dig inserts differs. Lab 3 breaks this link.VI: DS = băm của KSK vùng con, do vùng cha công bố và ký. Cùng key tag 30957, cùng digest — chỉ khác dấu cách dig chèn vào. Lab 3 làm gãy mắt xích này.

4. What anchors the whole chain?Cái gì neo cả chuỗi?
   Answer: b) The trust anchor: the root key hash set in the validator
   Everything else is checked; the anchor is trusted without proof. The real root has been signed since 15 July 2010.VI: Mọi thứ khác đều được kiểm; mỏ neo được tin mà không cần chứng minh. Gốc thật được ký từ 15/7/2010.

5. delv says "fully validated" for the CNAME and "unsigned answer" for labflow.cdn.test. Why?delv nói "fully validated" cho CNAME và "unsigned answer" cho labflow.cdn.test. Vì sao?
   Answer: d) cdn.test has no DS: provably unsigned, which is allowed
   Insecure ≠ bogus: there is a signed proof that no DS exists, so the validator accepts unsigned data for that zone.VI: Insecure ≠ bogus: có bằng chứng được ký rằng không có DS, nên bộ kiểm chấp nhận dữ liệu không ký cho vùng đó.

exercises.solutionExplanationHtml:
Answer key / Đáp án

  1. c) Expiration then inception of the signature, in UTC

    Order: covered type, algorithm (13 = ECDSA P-256), labels, original TTL, EXPIRATION, INCEPTION, key tag, signer, signature. Here valid for 30 days; someone (or a job) must re-sign before the end.

    VI: Thứ tự: loại được ký, thuật toán (13 = ECDSA P-256), số nhãn, TTL gốc, HẾT HẠN, BẮT ĐẦU, key tag, người ký, chữ ký. Ở đây hiệu lực 30 ngày; ai đó (hoặc một tác vụ) phải ký lại trước khi hết.

  2. a) 256 signs the records (ZSK); 257 signs the keys (KSK)

    The flags field: 257 has the SEP bit. Splitting the roles lets you change the ZSK often without touching the parent.

    VI: Trường flags: 257 có bit SEP. Tách vai trò giúp đổi ZSK thường xuyên mà không đụng tới vùng cha.

  3. d) The parent vouches for exactly the key that labflow.test publishes

    DS = hash of the child's KSK, published and signed by the parent. Same key tag 30957, same digest — only the space dig inserts differs. Lab 3 breaks this link.

    VI: DS = băm của KSK vùng con, do vùng cha công bố và ký. Cùng key tag 30957, cùng digest — chỉ khác dấu cách dig chèn vào. Lab 3 làm gãy mắt xích này.

  4. b) The trust anchor: the root key hash set in the validator

    Everything else is checked; the anchor is trusted without proof. The real root has been signed since 15 July 2010.

    VI: Mọi thứ khác đều được kiểm; mỏ neo được tin mà không cần chứng minh. Gốc thật được ký từ 15/7/2010.

  5. d) cdn.test has no DS: provably unsigned, which is allowed

    Insecure ≠ bogus: there is a signed proof that no DS exists, so the validator accepts unsigned data for that zone.

    VI: Insecure ≠ bogus: có bằng chứng được ký rằng không có DS, nên bộ kiểm chấp nhận dữ liệu không ký cho vùng đó.

# DNSSEC 2 — The order of the checks, and of the diagnosis — answer key

1. Order the checks a validating resolver makes for labflow.test A, starting from what it already trusts.Xếp các bước kiểm mà resolver kiểm DNSSEC làm cho labflow.test A, bắt đầu từ thứ nó đã tin.
   Answer: m2) The root DNSKEY matches the trust anchor  →  m1) The DS for test. is signed by the root  →  m4) test.'s DNSKEY matches that DS; the DS for labflow.test is signed by test.  →  m5) labflow.test's KSK (257) matches that DS and signs the DNSKEY set  →  m3) The ZSK (256) verifies the RRSIG over the A record
   Top-down from the anchor, one link per level. Fail at any step ⇒ bogus ⇒ SERVFAIL; a missing DS at some step (provably) ⇒ insecure from there down.VI: Từ mỏ neo đi xuống, mỗi cấp một mắt xích. Hỏng ở bước nào ⇒ bogus ⇒ SERVFAIL; thiếu DS (có chứng minh) ở bước nào ⇒ insecure từ đó trở xuống.

2. "Works on my machine, not on yours": order the six checks of the lesson."Máy tôi chạy, máy bạn không": xếp sáu bước kiểm của bài học.
   Answer: m3) What the app gets: getent ahosts name (hosts file, search domains)  →  m6) Which resolver: resolv.conf, resolvectl status  →  m5) Each resolver: dig name @resolver (old answer? TTL counting?)  →  m1) The truth: dig name @ns1 / @ns2 + SOA serial  →  m2) DNSSEC: compare with +cd and read the EDE  →  m4) Delegation: dig +trace (NXDOMAIN at the TLD, a slow hop)
   From the app outward: first what the program really sees, then each layer that could hold a different answer, until the authoritative servers and the delegation above them.VI: Từ ứng dụng ra ngoài: trước hết thứ chương trình thật sự thấy, rồi từng lớp có thể giữ câu trả lời khác, tới máy chủ có thẩm quyền và ủy quyền phía trên chúng.

3. Order the fix of the expired-signature incident.Xếp các bước sửa sự cố chữ ký hết hạn.
   Answer: m5) Confirm: SERVFAIL without +cd, the address with +cd, EDE 7  →  m2) Re-sign the zone correctly and bump the serial so ns2 copies it  →  m1) Check the new RRSIG window on the authoritative server  →  m3) Wait for (or flush) the bogus cache on resolvers — about 60 s on Unbound  →  m4) Add monitoring: alert when signatures expire in less than 7 days
   Diagnose before touching, fix at the source, verify on the authoritative server, then remember the caches. The last step is what kiem-dns.sh does in Lab 3.VI: Chẩn đoán trước khi động vào, sửa tận gốc, kiểm trên máy chủ có thẩm quyền, rồi nhớ tới cache. Bước cuối là việc kiem-dns.sh làm trong Lab 3.

   - r3.r: answer with ad

exercises.problemHtml:
The incident of the lesson in one function. A real RRSIG (lab/out/c35-chuoi) and the real moment of the incident (date -u in c35-hong: 20261101102450):

labflow.test.		300	IN	RRSIG	A 13 2 300 20261201102442 20261101092442 62671 labflow.test. tHgSYhKgL+Va+d31K7R/x1uYqtxMlg+HMxogV0sVgsGPq67oXpbYhlkk oaBIfTSTjL/5kmro5Hztjm8OCNprXg==

Write rrsigStatus(line, nowUtc, skew). line is a dig answer line of type RRSIG; after the word RRSIG come: covered type, algorithm, labels, original TTL, expiration, inception, key tag, signer, signature. Times are UTC YYYYMMDDHHMMSS. Return:

{ covers, algorithm, keyTag, signer, inception, expiration, status, daysLeft }
  • algorithm and keyTag are numbers; inception/expiration stay strings;

  • daysLeft = (expiration − now) in days, one decimal, negative when past.

Hidden cases: the incident's signature (expired two days before, rebuilt from the real fields c35-hong printed), the real cloudflare.com signature, and the one-day-skew trap the lesson describes.

Requirements

exercises.solutionExplanationHtml: A DNSSEC zone carries an expiry date on every record set; if the signing job dies, the zone breaks on a schedule, for everyone behind a validating resolver, while servers and network look healthy. exercises.title: DNSSEC 6 — Write dnsVerdict(): is it DNSSEC, the name, or the server?
exercises.problemHtml:
The fastest triage of a DNS failure needs two commands: dig name and dig +cd +short name. Real outputs (lab/out/c35-hong):

$ dig labflow.test | grep -E 'status|EDE'
;; ->>HEADER<<- opcode: QUERY, status: SERVFAIL, id: 14879
; EDE: 7 (Signature Expired): (validation failure <labflow.test. A IN>: signature expired from 203.0.113.53 for key labflow.test. while building chain of trust)
$ dig +cd +short labflow.test
203.0.113.10

Write dnsVerdict(plain, cdShort) returning { status, ede, cause }:

  • status — the word after status:, or null if there is none;
  • ede — from a line like ; EDE: 7 (Signature Expired): … ⇒ { code: 7, name: "Signature Expired" }, else null;
  • cause — "ok" for NOERROR, "no such name" for NXDOMAIN, for SERVFAIL "dnssec" when cdShort contains an IP address on a line of its own and "server failure" otherwise; with no status, "unreachable" if the text says "timed out" or "no servers could be reached", else "unknown"; any other status ⇒ "other".

Hidden cases, all real: dnssec-failed.org through 1.1.1.1 (EDE 9), Lab 3's incident B (EDE 6, DS ≠ key), a dead ns3 that times out, the expired domain oldshop.test, and a SERVFAIL whose +cd answer is empty.

Requirements

  • Return the value; do not print it.
  • Do not modify the arguments.
